verdict.rationale: Typesense Cloud's MCP server documentation says the user decides what a connected agent is allowed to do and can revoke the connection at any time. That is a first-party, agent-specific permission scoping mechanism, but the evidence never describes scoped API keys, their granularity, or the actions and collections they can be limited to. A 2020 community request for index-restricted keys shows the feature was absent then; it is historical and does not contradict the current claim. Missing for 10: documented scoped/least-privilege API key creation (per-collection, per-action restrictions), detail on what permissions the MCP connection can be limited to, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: You decide what it is allowed to do when you connect it, and you can disconnect it at any time.
Connect your AI agent to Typesense Cloud and it can create and configure clusters, build collections, index your data, tune search and read metrics, all from the conversation.
